week.weeklyOverview: This week toddlers meet the friendly Johnny Appleseed story through planting play, orchard pretend, seed discovery, and process art—not worksheets or tiny crafts. They dig, plant (with large cups), water with tiny watering cans, build big apple trees from recycled materials, and parade as kind seed-planters. Counting stays playful with large apple props. Life-cycle ideas use oversized picture cards for looking and talking, never paper sequencing quizzes. Soft cooked apple tasting stays optional and allergy-aware. The week is short-turn, sensory, and childcare-realistic.
week.objectives:
Social-emotional: Practice gentle care for plants/animals in story play and share orchard tools.
Language: Hear and try words such as seed, plant, water, grow, tree, orchard, harvest, and Johnny.
Cognitive: Notice seed → plant → tree → apple with large picture cards and real props.
Fine motor: Dig, scoop soil, glue large collage pieces, stamp apple prints.
Gross motor: Grow-tall movement, water dance, orchard parade.
Sensory: Soil/dry bean garden bins, apple smell, collage textures.
Creative: Process tree art, hat decorating, orchard collage—no “right” finished look.
week.weeklyMaterials:
Everyday: potting soil or clean play sand, large cups/pots, spoons, watering cans, baskets, smocks, trays, towels
Apple props: plastic/wood apples, large apple pictures, empty seed packets (sealed), real apple seeds ONLY in sealed discovery bags or teacher-supervised large trays (choking watch)
Art: washable paint, paper, glue sticks, brown paper, tissue, stickers, cardboard tubes, green scrap paper
Sensory: soil/beans/oats garden bin, scoops, artificial leaves/flowers
Dramatic play: baskets, wagons, orchard signs, simple hat bands
Literacy: My Little Golden Book About Johnny Appleseed; Little Naturalists: Johnny Appleseed; Johnny Appleseed (Reeve Lindbergh); Ten Red Apples; The Apple Pie Tree
Optional printables: oversized life-cycle picture cards; orchard zone signs; seed/plant/water choice cards
week.teacherPreparation:
Before Monday: allergy survey for apple; decide tasting plan.
Prep sealed seed discovery bags (real seeds sealed OR large craft “seeds”).
Fill sensory garden bin; pre-portion planting cups.
Print/cut oversized life-cycle cards (seed, sprout, tree, apple)—toddler-large, not tiny.
Pre-cut hat bands and tree collage materials.
Stage a reusable Orchard Corner that can stay all week.
Pull 2–3 Johnny/apple books; practice short story language (kindness, planting, walking).
prepChecklist: Complete apple allergy check with families
Stage Orchard Corner with baskets and signs
Pre-cut hat bands and tree collage scraps
Sanitize sensory tools; remove tiny pieces
week.observationFocus:
Interest in seed/plant talk
Tool sharing at garden bin
Willingness to dig/plant/water
Language attempts (seed, grow, tree, apple)
Process-art engagement without product pressure
Comfort with optional apple smelling/tasting
week.familyConnection: Invite families to notice an apple or tree on a walk and say “seed” or “grow” together. Optional: plant a bean or herb seed at home (easier than apple trees)—no required homework. Share that classroom tasting is always optional.
week.adaptations: Offer watching-first entry, dry sensory alternatives, larger handles, picture cards, and shorter turns. Never force tasting or dirt play. Provide sealed seed bags for children who mouth everything.

activities.title: Apple Seed Discovery
activities.objective: Explore apple seeds safely through looking, shaking sealed bags, and naming seed/apple with teacher support.
activities.description: Toddlers examine a cut apple (teacher-cut, displayed) and sealed seed discovery bags. They shake, look, and match large seed pictures—no loose tiny seeds for unsupervised play.
activities.materials:
Teacher-cut apple halves on tray (or clear display)
Sealed clear bags with a few apple seeds OR large craft seed props
Magnifying glasses (toddler-safe)
Picture cards: apple / seed
Smocks optional; wipes
activities.preparation: Teacher cuts apple before children arrive. Seal seeds in sturdy bags. Remove any loose small seeds from reach.
activities.setup: Low discovery table with apple display, sealed bags, and two picture cards. Soft mat for sitting.
activities.steps:
1. Gather 2–4 toddlers.
2. Show apple half; point to seeds—“Seeds live inside.”
3. Offer sealed bags to shake and look.
4. Match bag to seed picture card.
5. Narrate: seed can grow a tree someday.
6. All done: wash hands; put bags in basket.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Where are the seeds?
Can you shake, shake?
Are the seeds tiny or big?
Seeds help grow trees.
Can you find the apple picture?
We look with our eyes—gentle hands.
activities.observationOpportunities: Visual attention to seeds, vocabulary attempts, gentle handling, and interest in matching pictures.
activities.safetyNotes: Choking hazard: no loose small seeds for mouthing children. Teacher-only knife. Sanitize after handling display apple.
activities.cleanupTips: Bagreeze or discard display apple per policy; wipe table; store sealed bags.

activities.title: Johnny's Apple Tree
activities.objective: Create open-ended apple tree process art using stamps, collage, or paint—no required finished look.
activities.description: Toddlers paint or stamp apple shapes onto paper trees or brown trunks. Emphasize process: dipping, stamping, sticking leaves. Finished art looks child-made and uneven.
activities.materials:
Paper; brown crayon/marker trunks (pre-drawn optional)
Washable red/green/yellow paint
Apple halves or potato “apple” stamps (teacher-cut)
Tissue paper leaves; glue sticks
Smocks; trays
activities.preparation: Prep stamps; pour paint on trays; pre-draw simple trunks if helpful; cover table.
activities.setup: Art table with smocks, one tray per child, stamps and collage bits in reach.
activities.steps:
1. Put on smocks.
2. Show: “Johnny planted trees—we make tree pictures.”
3. Model one stamp or glue one leaf.
4. Invite free stamping/collage.
5. Name colors and actions.
6. Dry flat; wash hands.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Dip and stamp!
Where will your apple go?
Red apple, green leaf.
Your tree is growing!
More or all done?
Beautiful Johnny tree.
activities.observationOpportunities: Grip on stamp, color naming, persistence, and pride in process.
activities.safetyNotes: Non-toxic paint; supervise stamps; wipe mouths if paint is mouthed.
activities.cleanupTips: Soak stamps; wipe trays; hang art to dry.

activities.title: Count the Apple Seeds
activities.objective: Practice playful 1–3 counting with large seed props or sealed bags—not worksheets or tiny loose seeds.
activities.description: Toddlers place large seed props into muffin cups while teacher models counting to 1, 2, or 3. Keep it game-like and brief.
activities.materials:
Large craft seeds / wooden discs / laminated seed pictures
Muffin tin or 3 bowls
Number cards 1–3 with dots
Basket
activities.preparation: Set out only large props. Post 1–3 cards.
activities.setup: Floor or low table with muffin tin and seed basket.
activities.steps:
1. Show one seed—“One.”
2. Invite child to drop seeds into cups.
3. Count together aloud to 3 max.
4. Cheer and reset.
5. Offer another turn or all done.
activities.teacherLanguage:
One seed!
Can you put two?
Three seeds in the cup.
Shall we count again?
You did it!
activities.observationOpportunities: One-to-one dropping, attention to counting chant, turn-taking.
activities.safetyNotes: No small chokeable seeds. Supervise mouthing.

activities.title: Growing Apple Trees
activities.objective: Use whole-body movement to act out seed → sprout → tree → apple shake.
activities.description: Short movement story: curl as seeds, stretch as sprouts, stand tall as trees, gently “shake apples” down. Repeat 2–3 times.
activities.materials: Open floor space; optional soft music; picture cards for each stage
activities.preparation: Clear hazards; practice simple cues.
activities.setup: Circle or free space with cards visible on wall/floor.
activities.steps:
1. Show seed card—curl small.
2. Sprout—kneel and stretch arms.
3. Tree—stand tall, arms up.
4. Apples—gentle shake, then “pick” to basket.
5. Rest and repeat once.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Tiny seed… curl up!
Sprout up, up!
Tall apple tree!
Shake, shake the apples.
Pick an apple—yum!
Ready to grow again?
activities.observationOpportunities: Imitation of poses, balance, enjoyment, following sequence cues.
activities.safetyNotes: Space for movement; no climbing furniture; gentle shaking only.

activities.objective: Practice simple planting: scoop soil, place a seed prop or large bean, cover, and water with a tiny can.

activities.materials:
Large cups/pots; potting soil or clean play sand
Spoons; large beans or supervised seeds

Trays; smocks; name stickers

2. Scoop soil into cup.

activities.safetyNotes: Choking watch for seeds/beans. No standing water. Soil not for eating—redirect. Outdoor soil policies per center.

activities.title: Healthy Apple Trees
activities.objective: Explore what trees need (sun, water, soil, care) using picture cards and real props—simple and concrete.
activities.description: Toddlers match care cards to props: watering can, sun picture, soil cup, gentle hands. Talk about kind care like Johnny.
activities.materials:
Cards: sun, water, soil, gentle hands
Props: watering can, flashlight “sun,” soil cup, soft cloth
Small plant or tree picture
activities.preparation: Print care cards; gather props.
activities.setup: Discovery rug with plant picture in center and props around.
activities.steps:
1. Show tree—“Trees need care.”
2. Match water card to can.
3. Match sun to flashlight glow (brief).
4. Touch soil cup.
5. Practice gentle pat on stuffed animal/tree prop.
6. Retell needs together.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Trees need water.
Trees need sun.
Trees need soil.
Gentle hands care.
We can help trees.
Johnny was kind to trees.
activities.observationOpportunities: Matching interest, gentle touch, care vocabulary.
activities.safetyNotes: Flashlight not in eyes; soil not eaten; supervise.

activities.adaptations: Pre-glued grass; child adds apples only.
activities.extensions: Add photo of each child as orchard helper.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older place more detailed trees; younger stick apples.

activities.title: Apple Orchard Collage
activities.objective: Create a group or individual orchard collage with textured papers and apple shapes.
activities.description: Toddlers glue torn paper, fabric scraps, and apple cutouts onto mural or individual papers to build a busy orchard scene.
activities.materials:
Large mural paper or individual sheets
Torn green/brown/red papers; fabric scraps
Glue sticks; apple stickers
Smocks
activities.preparation: Tear papers; hang mural at toddler height if group.
activities.setup: Collage station with bowls of scraps.
activities.steps:
1. Show empty orchard paper.
2. Glue “grass” and “trees.”
3. Add apples freely.
4. Stand back and name friends’ trees.
5. Dry and display.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Tear the paper—rip rip!
Glue a tree.
Add apples.
Our orchard is full!
Whose tree is this?
Beautiful work together.
activities.observationOpportunities: Tearing/gluing, collaboration near peers, color choices.
activities.safetyNotes: Non-toxic glue; supervise small stickers.

activities.decisionNote: Priority 1 Pro upgrade — substantial Teaching Kit rewrite (draft only); toddler-safe Johnny Appleseed/orchard focus
activities.adaptations: Seated motions; picture cue cards for each action.
activities.extensions: Children choose next action card.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants bounce to rhythm; toddlers do motions.
activities.title: Orchard Workers Song
activities.objective: Sing/chant orchard worker actions with motions: pick, carry, wash, rest.
activities.description: Simple original/traditional-style chant with motions. Do not reproduce copyrighted lyrics; use LLH chant and public-domain frames.
activities.materials: Optional baskets; music optional; lyric card for teacher (original chant)
activities.preparation: Learn LLH chant; clear space.
activities.setup: Standing circle with baskets in center optional.
activities.steps:
1. Teach motions: pick, carry, wash, rest.
2. Chant once with teacher lead.
3. Children join motions.
4. Add basket pass.
5. Bow and done.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Pick, pick apples.
Carry the basket.
Wash, wash apples.
Orchard workers rest.
Again?
Great teamwork!
activities.observationOpportunities: Motion imitation, rhythm, peer awareness.
activities.safetyNotes: No running with baskets; safe spacing.

activities.title: Apple Tree Life Cycle Review
activities.objective: Retell the week’s growth story with cards and classroom props as a joyful review—not a quiz.
activities.description: Revisit seed → sprout → tree → apple using cards plus real classroom planting cups and orchard props. Children help tell the story.
activities.materials: Life-cycle cards; children’s planted cups; plastic apple; watering can
activities.preparation: Gather week props into a review basket.
activities.setup: Circle with props displayed.
activities.steps:
1. Show planted cups—“We planted.”
2. Move through cards with child helpers.
3. Water pretend/real carefully.
4. End with apple pick cheer.
5. Optional: one book page peek.
activities.teacherLanguage:
What did we plant?
What do seeds need?
Our trees are growing.
Who can find the apple card?
We cared like Johnny.
What was your favorite?
activities.observationOpportunities: Recall interest, prop use, preference sharing.
activities.safetyNotes: Same as earlier planting/card safety.

activities.title: Johnny Appleseed Hat
activities.objective: Decorate a simple wearable hat band for the parade—process decorating, not a perfect craft replica.
activities.description: Toddlers sticker, stamp, or color a pre-cut hat band / paper crown. Optional tin-pot pretend prop for teacher storytelling only if safe and not forced as costume.
activities.materials:
Pre-cut paper hat bands; tape/stapler (teacher)
Stickers, dot markers, apple stamps
Smocks optional
activities.preparation: Pre-cut bands to size; portion decorations.
activities.setup: Art table with bands labeled; decorations in bowls.
activities.steps:
1. Choose a band.
2. Decorate freely.
3. Teacher fit/tape to size.
4. Try on briefly.
5. Store for parade.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Decorate your Johnny hat!
Sticker here?
Dot dot dot.
Ready to try it on?
You look ready to plant seeds.
Hats rest until parade.
activities.observationOpportunities: Decorating choices, tolerance for wearing, pride.
activities.safetyNotes: Teacher-only stapler; watch for mouthing stickers; optional wear—never force.

activities.adaptations: Collect any apples without number demand; then count together.
activities.extensions: Color sort after counting.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older match numeral; younger use dots only.
activities.title: Apple Orchard Counting Challenge
activities.objective: Play a brief orchard counting game collecting large apples into baskets up to 3–5.
activities.description: Scatter large apples in play orchard. Toddlers collect a requested small number into baskets. Keep playful—no timed tests.
activities.materials:
Large plastic/paper apples; baskets; 1–5 cards
Open floor orchard area
activities.preparation: Scatter apples; set cards.
activities.setup: Defined orchard zone with baskets at start line.
activities.steps:
1. Show card “2.”
2. Collect two apples.
3. Count into basket together.
4. Return apples and try new number.
5. Cheer effort.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Can you find two apples?
Put them in the basket.
Let’s count—1, 2!
Try three?
Fast walking feet—safe.
You did the challenge!
activities.observationOpportunities: Number response, searching, returning materials.
activities.safetyNotes: Walking feet; large apples only; clear floor.

teacherTips: Keep parade under 3 minutes of walking.
Offer wagon rides for children who fatigue.
activities.adaptations: Seated parade with arm marching; shorter route.
activities.extensions: Family hallway parade at pickup (optional).
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants strolled along; toddlers march; preschool carry signs.

activities.title: Johnny Appleseed Parade
activities.objective: Celebrate the week with a short indoor/outdoor parade as kind seed planters—music, hats, and gentle marching.
activities.description: Toddlers wear optional hats, carry seed packets (empty/sealed) or baskets, and parade to a simple march chant. End with a kindness cheer and book peek.
activities.materials:
Hats from art; baskets/empty seed envelopes
Music or drum; parade route markers
Johnny book for closing
activities.preparation: Clear route; gather hats; choose music.
activities.setup: Line-up spots with picture feet; end at story rug.
activities.steps:
1. Put on optional hats.
2. Give baskets/seed envelopes.
3. March slowly on route.
4. Pause to “plant” pretend seeds once.
5. End on rug for cheer + book cover look.
6. Photos optional for families.
activities.teacherLanguage:
March, march, planters!
Gentle feet.
Plant a seed—pat pat.
We are kind like Johnny.
Hooray for our orchard week!
Hats off—rest time.
activities.observationOpportunities: Group following, pride, stamina, closing attention.
activities.safetyNotes: Slow march; no running; outdoor sun/safety checks; optional costumes.
